title: Three beats against two lock together on a hidden grid of six
body: A polyrhythm plays two rhythms at once that don’t simply grow out of each other. The classic is 3 against 2: three evenly spaced beats and two evenly spaced beats in the same stretch of time, also called a hemiola. To count it, cut the time into the lowest common multiple of 3 and 2, which is 6. The threes land on steps 1, 3 and 5, the twos on 1 and 4, and together they make the rhythm of the phrase “not difficult”.

slides.alt: Animation of a drum head with two rotating rings: three coral markers and two cyan markers flash as they pass a strike point. A six-step grid shows the three on steps 1, 3 and 5 and the two on 1 and 4, the words “not difficult” land on the combined hits, and a 4-against-3 grid of 12 follows.
slides.music: “Journey To Ascend” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.prompt: Play 3 against 2 and watch where the beats fall on the six steps. Then try 4 against 3, or switch to tapping the slower rhythm yourself.
slides.takeaway: Two even rhythms fit on a grid of their lowest common multiple: 6 steps for 3 against 2, 12 for 4 against 3, 20 for 5 against 4. Count the grid and each hand taps its own steps.

slides.heading: Try it on a table
slides.text: Count six quick steps: 1 2 3 4 5 6. Your right hand taps 1, 3 and 5; your left taps 1 and 4. Speed up and you are playing three against two, with hits on 1, 3, 4 and 5.

slides.heading: Written as a triplet
slides.text: In written music, the three can be shown as a triplet: three notes squeezed into the time of two ordinary ones, each two-thirds of its usual length, marked with a small 3.

slides.heading: Where it runs deep
slides.text: The 3:2 relationship and its variations are the foundation of most typical polyrhythmic textures in West African music, and 3:2 is also listed among the common polyrhythms of jazz.

slides.heading: Which phrase doesn’t fit the 3-against-2 rhythm?
slides.explanation: The others have four syllables that fall on steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the six-step grid. “Happy birthday to you” has six syllables, too many for the four hits.

slides.question: Using the same trick, how many equal steps do you need to count 5 against 4?
slides.explanation: The grid is the lowest common multiple: 20 is the smallest number that both 5 and 4 divide evenly, so the fives land every 4 steps and the fours every 5.
